title: Energy Efficient Dual Designs of FeFET-Based Analog In-Memory Computing with Inherent Shift-Add Capability
problem: Existing analog in-memory computing designs have throughput limitations in the shift-add process: digital implementations suffer from ADC time-multiplexing bottlenecks, while analog domain implementations require customized circuits that compromise energy and area efficiency. The joint optimization of partial MAC operations and weight shift-add processes is rarely explored.
motivation: Improving energy efficiency of multiply-and-accumulate operations in deep neural networks by integrating computation within memory arrays.
method: The design uses ferroelectric FETs (transistors that store analog values using ferroelectric material properties) for in-memory computing—performing multiply-accumulate operations (repeated multiplication and addition) directly in memory columns. It naturally integrates the shift-add process (bit-shifting and summing weighted values) for 4-bit weights without needing separate circuits. Supporting both 2's complement and non-2's complement modes enables flexible handling of 4- or 8-bit weight data, with two implementations: CurFe for current-mode operation and ChgFe for charge-mode operation, both optimized for high-precision analog calculations.
key_novelty: Ferroelectric transistors (FeFETs, which store analog values) naturally combine in-memory computing (performing calculations where data is stored) with shift-add processing (bit-shifting and summing weights), eliminating the need for separate shift-add circuits.
contributions: FeFET-based IMC paradigm with inherent shift-add capability for 4-bit weights leveraging analog storage properties
Dual-mode support (2's complement and non-2's complement) enabling flexible 4-/8-bit weight formats
Two optimized circuit designs: CurFe (current-mode) and ChgFe (charge-mode) for high-precision analog IMC
Demonstrated 1.56× circuit-level and 1.37× system-level energy efficiency improvement over state-of-the-art

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 1.56× (circuit level) / 1.37× (system level) improvement vs state-of-the-art analog IMC

limitations: Design trade-offs and limitations of the proposed approach are not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: FeFET-based analog in-memory computing with integrated shift-add capability
